endorsements.quote: Ensuring all models— whether AI-based or mechanistic — are trained on diverse and comprehensive datasets is therefore critical to mitigate biases and promote equitable healthcare outcomes 36.

unlisted_practices: Develop regulatory frameworks that evolve alongside technological advancements and set rigorous standards for validating, interpreting, and approving AI and digital twin technologies.
Use propensity score matching and inverse probability weighting when training digital twins on observational datasets to balance covariates and reduce confounding bias.
Develop transparent, disease-specific validation pipelines that benchmark digital twin performance at scale.
Couple attention-based transformers and multimodal graph neural networks with explainability overlays to provide interpretable outputs.
Develop regulatory-grade uncertainty quantification for AI and digital twin models.
Establish robust data management that provides provenance transparency for data and models in AI and digital twins.
Use standardized AI model reporting pipelines such as CONSORT-AI and DECIDE-AI.
Create collaborative regulatory sandboxes to trial new AI frameworks under FDA/EMA oversight.
Exercise caution when using LLMs in patient-facing domains such as informed consent, and apply rigorous validation, regulatory oversight, and transparency.
Implement LLM-driven solutions alongside inclusive policies that address disparities in healthcare access.
Develop dynamic consent platforms using LLMs.
Implement safeguards to identify and mitigate unintended risks from AI agents.
